features.title: Scientific-Grade InGaAs Detector
features.description: ZephIR™ 1.7 uses an InGaAs detector designed for SWIR imaging. The detector architecture is suited to applications requiring sensitive infrared imaging across the 0.9–1.7 µm range.

features.title: Deep Four-Stage TEC Cooling
features.description: The camera uses a four-stage thermoelectric cooler capable of maintaining temperatures as low as −80 °C. Deep cooling is a key part of the camera's low-noise imaging design.

features.title: Extremely Low Noise
features.description: Photon etc. describes ZephIR™ 1.7 as having extremely low noise levels. This makes the camera suitable for applications where weak infrared signals need to be detected and characterized.

features.title: High Efficiency
features.description: The camera combines high efficiency with its scientific-grade InGaAs detector and low-noise architecture.

features.title: Rapid Frame Rate
features.description: ZephIR™ 1.7 provides a rapid frame rate, allowing it to be used for applications where fast image acquisition is required.

features.title: External Trigger Compatibility
features.description: The camera supports an external trigger, enabling synchronized image acquisition within experimental or automated imaging systems.

features.title: Forced-Air Cooling
features.description: The TEC uses forced-air cooling. This eliminates the need for a separate water or liquid-nitrogen chiller unit and simplifies camera integration.

faqs.question: What is ZephIR™ 1.7?
faqs.answer: ZephIR™ 1.7 is a scientific-grade InGaAs SWIR camera from Photon etc. designed for sensitive infrared imaging across 0.9–1.7 µm.

faqs.question: What wavelength range does ZephIR™ 1.7 cover?
faqs.answer: ZephIR™ 1.7 is sensitive from 0.9 to 1.7 µm.

faqs.question: How cold can ZephIR™ 1.7 operate?
faqs.answer: The camera uses a four-stage thermoelectric cooler capable of maintaining an operating temperature as low as −80 °C.

faqs.question: What cooling method does ZephIR™ 1.7 use?
faqs.answer: The camera uses four-stage TEC cooling with forced air.

faqs.question: Does ZephIR™ 1.7 require liquid nitrogen?
faqs.answer: No. The supplied manufacturer information states that its forced-air TEC cooling removes the need for a liquid-nitrogen chiller unit.

faqs.question: Does ZephIR™ 1.7 require water cooling?
faqs.answer: No. The forced-air cooling system eliminates the need for a water chiller unit.

faqs.question: What is ZephIR™ 1.7 used for?
faqs.answer: Applications identified by Photon etc. include NIR-II/SWIR bio-imaging, photovoltaic characterization using PL and EL, semiconductor wafer inspection and device failure detection.

faqs.question: Can ZephIR™ 1.7 be used for photovoltaic characterization?
faqs.answer: Yes. Photon etc. identifies photoluminescence and electroluminescence imaging for photovoltaic characterization as an application.

faqs.question: Can ZephIR™ 1.7 be used for semiconductor inspection?
faqs.answer: Yes. The camera is positioned for semiconductor wafer inspection and device failure detection.

faqs.question: Does ZephIR™ 1.7 support external triggering?
faqs.answer: Yes. The manufacturer describes the camera as compatible with an external trigger.

faqs.question: Is ZephIR™ 1.7 a SWIR camera?
faqs.answer: Yes. Photon etc. categorizes ZephIR™ 1.7 as a SWIR camera and describes it as a scientific-grade InGaAs camera.

faqs.question: What is the difference between ZephIR™ 1.7 and ZephIR™ 2.5e?
faqs.answer: ZephIR™ 1.7 covers 0.9–1.7 µm and uses an InGaAs detector, while ZephIR™ 2.5e extends to 2.5 µm and uses a T2SL focal plane array. The appropriate camera depends on the required spectral range and application.

faqs.answer: Pricing depends on the configuration and application requirements. Contact Inkarp for a quotation.

faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for Photon etc. ZephIR™ 1.7 in India.

longForm.heroHook: Deep-Cooled InGaAs SWIR Camera for 0.9–1.7 µm Imaging
longForm.heroLead: Scientific-grade SWIR imaging with extremely low noise, high efficiency and deep thermoelectric cooling to −80 °C. Photon etc. ZephIR™ 1.7 is a scientific-grade InGaAs SWIR camera designed for high-sensitivity infrared imaging and demanding research applications. The camera combines Photon etc.'s control electronics with a four-stage thermoelectric cooler (TEC) capable of maintaining an operating temperature as low as −80 °C. Forced-air cooling removes the need for a water or liquid-nitrogen chiller unit. ZephIR™ 1.7 is designed for applications including NIR-II/SWIR bio-imaging, photovoltaic characterization using photoluminescence (PL) and electroluminescence (EL), semiconductor wafer inspection and device failure detection.

sections.eyebrow: Why Deep Cooling Matters in SWIR Imaging
sections.title: Why Deep Cooling Matters in SWIR Imaging
body: Reduce detector noise for sensitive measurements
SWIR imaging applications can involve weak optical signals. Detector temperature can influence unwanted noise and therefore affect the quality of acquired images.
ZephIR™ 1.7 uses a four-stage thermoelectric cooler capable of maintaining an operating temperature as low as −80 °C.
The deep cooling is designed to support the camera's low-noise performance while avoiding the infrastructure associated with water or liquid-nitrogen cooling.

groups.title: Spectral Range
body: ZephIR™ 1.7 covers wavelengths from 0.9 to 1.7 µm.
This range is relevant to applications where NIR-II and SWIR spectral information is required.

groups.title: NIR-II / SWIR Bio-Imaging
groups.description: Deep-cooled imaging for NIR-II and SWIR research
body: ZephIR™ 1.7 is positioned for NIR-II/SWIR bio-imaging.
Its 0.9–1.7 µm sensitivity and deep-cooled InGaAs detector provide a platform for imaging applications that operate in this spectral region.
The low-noise design is particularly relevant when imaging applications require sensitive detection of weak signals.

groups.title: Photovoltaic Characterization
body: ZephIR™ 1.7 can be used for photovoltaic characterization through photoluminescence (PL) and electroluminescence (EL) imaging.
These imaging methods can help researchers investigate spatial variations and emission behaviour across photovoltaic materials and devices.

groups.title: Semiconductor Wafer Inspection
body: ZephIR™ 1.7 is designed for semiconductor wafer inspection.
SWIR imaging can provide information beyond visible imaging, making the camera relevant to inspection workflows involving semiconductor materials and devices.

groups.title: Device Failure Detection
groups.description: Identify infrared signatures associated with device failures
body: ZephIR™ 1.7 is also positioned for device failure detection.
Its low-noise InGaAs imaging capability and rapid frame rate support inspection workflows where spatial infrared information is required to investigate device behaviour or failure.
